---
title: "Examples"
description: "Short notebooks that open large ocean datasets as virtual Icechunk stores, and ideas for your own questions."
---

Each example opens a large ocean dataset as a **virtual Icechunk store** and
answers one question with it in a few seconds or minutes. You download nothing
in advance, even when the dataset is hundreds of terabytes or thousands of files.
Use them to see how a store opens, how much a read costs, and what kind of
analysis becomes easy. Each one has an **Open in Colab** button.

| | Dataset | What it shows | Read time |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1](01-hycom-snow-crab.ipynb) | HYCOM reanalysis, 306 TB | Bering Sea bottom temperature on the snow crab grounds | seconds |
| [2](02-pacioos-aloha-profiles.ipynb) | PacIOOS ROMS Hawaiʻi reanalysis | How deep the seasons reach; water masses in T–S | ~15 s |
| [3](03-oa-saturation-horizon.ipynb) | NCEI ocean acidification indicators | The aragonite saturation horizon | seconds |
| [4](04-oisst-world-sst.ipynb) | NOAA OISST, ~16,500 daily files | Daily world SST, one line per year since 1981 | ~40 s |
| [5](05-oisst-gulf-of-maine-heatwaves.ipynb) | NOAA OISST, every daily file | Marine heatwave days in the Gulf of Maine | ~3 min |
| [6](06-gobai-oxygen-minimum-zone.ipynb) | GOBAI HR oxygen, weekly 1993–2025 | The eastern tropical Pacific oxygen minimum zone | seconds |

Times were measured on the workshop's JupyterHub; elsewhere they can be longer.

## Try your own questions

The examples are starting points. Each store holds far more than one notebook
uses. Here are some questions to try:

- **HYCOM:** how does the Bering Sea cold pool's extent change from year to
  year? How do currents through the Aleutian passes vary?
- **PacIOOS:** how big is the tide at Honolulu? Can you see the afternoon
  surface warming in calm summer weeks?
- **OA indicators:** where are pH and aragonite saturation lowest at the
  surface? Which regions have the fewest observations behind the map?
- **OISST:** in which year was your favourite stretch of coast warmest? How
  does the Niño 3.4 index line up with the world SST chart?
- **GOBAI:** is the oxygen minimum zone of the Arabian Sea or off Peru changing
  too? Where does nitrate track oxygen?

## Ask your agent

You do not need to write the code. Give your agent the store's URL and a
question, and ask it to tell you what it will read before it reads it.

| Store | URL | README |
|---|---|---|
| HYCOM GOFS 3.1 reanalysis | `https://data.source.coop/ocean-icechunks/hycom/hycom-gofs-3pt1-reanalysis` | [README](https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/hycom/tree/main/hycom-gofs-3pt1-reanalysis) |
| PacIOOS ROMS Hawaiʻi reanalysis | `https://data.source.coop/ocean-icechunks/pacioos/roms_hiig_reanalysis/icechunk` | [README](https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/pacioos/tree/main/stores/roms_hiig_reanalysis) |
| NCEI OA indicators | `https://data.source.coop/ocean-icechunks/oa-indicators/climatology` | [README](https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/icechunks/tree/main/oa-indicators) |
| NOAA OISST v2.1 | `https://data.source.coop/ocean-icechunks/noaa-oisst/oisst.icechunk` | [README](https://github.com/ocean-icechunks/noaa_oisst) |
| GOBAI HR | `gs://noaa-oar-gobai/icechunk/v202606` | [page](https://storage.googleapis.com/noaa-oar-gobai/index.html) |

A sample prompt:

> Open the virtual Icechunk store at
> `https://data.source.coop/ocean-icechunks/noaa-oisst/oisst.icechunk`
> anonymously. Its data are virtual references to NOAA's files, so authorize
> anonymous reads of the store's virtual chunk containers. List its groups and
> variables, and explain how the arrays are chunked.
>
> Then answer this question: **in which year was the sea surface off Cape Cod
> warmest, and on which day?** Before you read any data, tell me how many chunks
> and roughly how many bytes your plan reads. If there is a cheaper way, say so.
> Then write a short notebook with one figure, and run it.

Two parts of that prompt do most of the work:

- **"Tell me what you will read first."** A careless read of a big store can
  pull gigabytes; a good plan for the same question might pull megabytes.
- **"Explain the chunking."** How a store is chunked decides which questions
  are cheap. A map at one time step and a long time series at one point can
  differ in cost by a thousand times.

If the agent gets stuck opening a store, give it the store's README link from
the table above: each README has working code to open that store.
